newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says DKB arrests "grave beyond words".
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says DKB arrests "grave beyond words".

text.p: The arrests of four Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank officials on suspicion of violating the Commercial Code on Thursday are "grave and beyond words", Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a regular news conference on Friday.
Asked about his opinion on the arrests, Mitsuzuka said: "The fact that the officials have been arrested is very grave beyond words."
The finance minister said his ministry will take strict measures against DKB, taking into account the ongoing investigation by prosecutors.
"If further judiciary measures are taken, then we will take strict measures," Mitsuzuka said.
He added that the ministry was closely following the prosecutors' investigation. MOF has also asked DKB to submit a report on the issue to the ministry.
Asked if DKB vice-president Ichiro Fujita should not take over as the bank's new president as planned, Mitsuzuka said the issue of responsibility of officials was up to the bank itself.

Prosecutors have begun searching the headquarters of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd for evidence connected to suspected illegal payments to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer, Jiji news agency reported on Friday.
Mitsuzuka said the ministry will consider carrying out non-routine inspections of banks from now on to ensure that such incidents do not recur.
He said that, since it was difficult to learn the conditions of banks through regular inspections, "we will carry out non-routine inspections appropriately".
Currently the ministry conducts inspections at regular intervals.

Mitsuzuka also said the ministry had informed overseas authorities about the suspected illegal dealings by DKB and Nomura Securities Co Ltd through the ministry's regular contacts with officials from the Group of Seven (G7) nations.
